title: Finite-level residue sequences on an open curve
statement:
Let $C_0/\mathbf F_q$ be a smooth projective geometrically connected
curve, let $D_0\subset C_0$ be a finite reduced closed subscheme, and put
$U_0=C_0-D_0$. After base change to
$\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, write $j:U\hookrightarrow C$ and
$i:D\hookrightarrow C$. Put $A_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, with $\ell$ prime and
$\ell\ne\operatorname{char}\mathbf F_q$. For every $n\geq1$, there is
a Frobenius-equivariant exact sequence

$$
0\longrightarrow H^1(C,A_n)\xrightarrow{j^*}H^1(U,A_n)
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{res}_n}H^0(D,A_n(-1))
\longrightarrow H^2(C,A_n).
\tag{5.1}
$$

The sequences and their transition maps in $n$ are compatible. There
is $m\geq1$ such that, for $Q=q^m$, $\Phi_Q$ fixes every geometric
point of $D$; on the inverse-limit boundary module

$$
\varprojlim_n H^0(D,A_n(-1))
$$

it acts as multiplication by $Q$, and this module has no nonzero
$\Phi_Q$-fixed element. Here the finite-field datum is [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a smooth projective curve means [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve], and geometric connectedness means that its base change to the algebraic closure is connected. Finite morphisms and reduced schemes have the meanings of [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. The displayed groups are ordinary etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], equivalently the cohomology of their finite constant-coefficient pullbacks to the small pro-etale site by [sk-prop-sf-comparison]. Twists are [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], with canonical Weil structures [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. Frobenius is the geometric Galois automorphism of [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]; its operator on finite-coefficient cohomology is $H^r(R\Gamma(\theta)\circ\tau)$, with $\tau$ the finite-coefficient transport of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. The inverse limit means compatible tuples under coefficient reduction, with Frobenius acting coordinatewise.

proof.text: The boundary is a finite disjoint union of geometric points. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] makes $D\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ finite and $D$ affine. The finite field $k_0$ is perfect: its injective map $a\mapsto a^p$ is surjective on the finite set $k_0$. Thus [lem-kun-geometric-reduced-perfect] makes $D$ reduced. Finiteness makes $D$ proper over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-reduced-algclosed-global-sections-product] to $D$: for a finite set $I$, $\Gamma(D,\mathcal O_D)\cong\prod_{x\in I}k$. Since $D$ is affine, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-finite-product-fields] identifies $D$ with $\coprod_{x\in I}\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its local rings are fields, hence regular of dimension zero (their maximal ideals are zero). The empty boundary corresponds to $I=\varnothing$.

source.place: First paragraph, first sentence: the geometric boundary is a finite disjoint union of closed points

proof.text:
The geometric curve $C$ is smooth of relative dimension one by [lem-sc-curve-base-change-relative-dimension-one], and is connected by geometric connectedness of $C_0$. By [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings] it is Noetherian, and its local rings at the points of $D$ are discrete valuation rings of dimension one. At any such point $x$, removing the other finitely many closed points identifies $D$ locally with the reduced point $x$. Its ideal is generated by one non-zero-divisor by [lem-sc-point-cartier]. Together with $\dim\mathcal O_{C,x}=1$ and $\dim\mathcal O_{D,x}=0$, this verifies exactly the regular-sequence and pure-codimension-one conditions of [def-pur-regular-immersion]. With $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, $\varpi_E=\ell$ and $\Lambda=A_n$, [thm-pur-regular-immersion-purity] therefore gives the canonical isomorphism
$$P_n:Ri^!A_{n,C}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{n,D}(-1)[-2].$$
The ambient field $k$ is algebraically closed, hence perfect, and $\ell$ is invertible on both schemes. For empty $D$ the assertion is the unique isomorphism between zero objects. By [prop-pur-regular-immersion-purity-compatibilities] these isomorphisms respect finite reduction and etale base change.

source.place: First paragraph, Cartier argument, (5.2), and finite-reduction sentence

proof.text: Identify the exceptional functor in purity with the closed-support functor, keeping the counit. Write $H=A_{n,C_{\mathrm{et}}}$, $S=\nu^*$, $U=R\nu_*$ and $I_{\mathrm{et}}=Ri^!_{\mathrm{et}}$. The finite transported exceptional functor is $J=S_D I_{\mathrm{et}}U_C$ by [lem-coef-site-closed-counit-transport]. For this bounded degree-zero etale $H$, that node gives $\alpha_H:S_DI_{\mathrm{et}}H\xrightarrow{\sim}JS_CH$, with its displayed counit equation. The canonical isomorphism $\beta_H:S_DI_{\mathrm{et}}H\xrightarrow{\sim}I_{\mathrm{pro}}S_CH$ and its counit equation are [lem-weil-finite-duality-closed-comparison]. Hence $\beta_H\alpha_H^{-1}:JS_CH\xrightarrow{\sim}I_{\mathrm{pro}}S_CH$ respects the supported counit. By [lem-exc-proetale-closed-support], $I_{\mathrm{pro}}$ is the derived supported-kernel functor. We may therefore use the isomorphism $P_n$ of step 2 for this functor; this comparison concerns the bounded etale-origin constant object, and asserts no ambient exceptional adjunction for general morphisms.

source.place: First paragraph, the identification of the purity and support functors implicit between (5.2) and (5.3)

proof.text:
The open complement $j$ is quasi-compact, since $C$ is Noetherian. The right adjoint $i^!$ of the exact functor $i_*$ in [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle] sends injectives to injectives: for injective $J$, $\operatorname{Hom}(-,i^!J)=\operatorname{Hom}(i_*(-),J)$ is exact. On a bounded-below injective resolution $A_{n,C}\to J^\bullet$, [def-pur-flasque-support] identifies $i_*i^!J^\bullet$ with the supported kernel sheaf. Taking sections therefore gives
$$\Gamma_D(C,J^\bullet)=\Gamma(D,i^!J^\bullet).$$
By the definition [def-pur-support-cohomology], these same complexes compute $R\Gamma_D(C,A_n)$ and $R\Gamma(D,Ri^!A_n)$. Substituting $P_n$ from step 2 yields
$$H_D^r(C,A_n)\cong H^{r-2}(D,A_n(-1)).$$
In particular $H_D^1(C,A_n)=0$ and $H_D^2(C,A_n)\cong H^0(D,A_n(-1))$: a sheaf in degree zero has zero negative cohomology, since its bounded-below injective resolution may start in degree zero.

source.place: First paragraph, (5.3) and the two supported-cohomology identifications

proof.text:
Apply [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] to the torsion coefficient sheaf $A_n$ and the pair $(C,D)$, on the pro-etale site. The segment in degrees one and two, using step 4, is
$$0\longrightarrow H^1(C,A_n)\xrightarrow{j^*}H^1(U,A_n)\longrightarrow H_D^2(C,A_n)\longrightarrow H^2(C,A_n).$$
Define $\operatorname{res}_n$ as the connecting map followed by the identification $H_D^2(C,A_n)\cong H^0(D,A_n(-1))$ of step 4. This is the asserted exact sequence. The groups for $C,U,D$ agree with etale cohomology by [sk-prop-sf-comparison], applied to the degree-zero discrete coefficient sheaves. No exactness of an inverse-limit functor is used.

source.place: First paragraph, degree-one part of (5.3) is (5.1)

proof.text: Both compatibilities concern the very maps just constructed. The automorphisms $g_C,g_D,g_U$ of [def-weil-frobenius-detailed] preserve the pair and commute with its inclusions. They are isomorphisms, hence etale. Functoriality in the pair and in the torsion sheaf in [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] makes the supported connecting map commute with these transports. Etale base-change compatibility in [prop-pur-regular-immersion-purity-compatibilities] makes $P_n$ commute with them as well. Thus their composite $\operatorname{res}_n$ commutes with the finite-coefficient Frobenius operators $H^r(R\Gamma(\theta)\circ\tau)$ of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport], with the canonical twist structure [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. For $A_{n+1}\to A_n$, apply the same functoriality in the torsion sheaf, together with the finite-reduction clause of the purity compatibility node: it gives the commuting square between the two connecting maps followed by $P_{n+1},P_n$. The other arrows are restrictions or supported counits and are functorial too. This gives a morphism of the displayed sequences at each reduction; iterating gives every transition. Here coefficient maps are maps of torsion sheaves after forgetting scalars; no flatness of $A_n$ over $A_{n+1}$ is asserted.

source.place: First paragraph, last sentence: Frobenius equivariance and compatibility under reduction

proof.text:
The automorphism $g_D$ permutes the finite set $I$ of points. If $I$ is nonempty choose $m\geq1$ divisible by all its cycle lengths; for $I=\varnothing$ take $m=1$. Then $g_D^m=\Phi_Q$, $Q=q^m$, preserves each component. Its restriction to the component $\operatorname{Spec}k$ lies over $\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma^m)$, so it is this semilinear automorphism, even though it fixes the underlying point. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-geometric-point-coproduct-cohomology] and [sk-prop-sf-comparison],
$$H^0(D,A_n(-1))\cong\prod_{x\in I}H^0(\operatorname{Spec}k,A_n(-1)).$$
Apply [lem-pur-twist-frobenius-scalar] with twist $-1$ and iterate its operator $m$ times: on each preserved component $\Phi_Q$ acts as $q^m=Q\pmod{\ell^n}$. Thus it acts as $Q$ on the entire product. The reduction identifications of that lemma give, from any generator $e$ of the free rank-one module $H^0(\operatorname{Spec}k,\mathbf Z_\ell(-1))$, compatible generators $e_n$. Hence these boundary groups and reduction maps identify with $A_n^I$ and coordinatewise reduction. On compatible tuples $\Phi_Q$ is consequently multiplication by $Q$.

source.place: Second paragraph, permutation of the points and scalar action on the boundary

proof.text: Let $r=(r_n)$ be a $\Phi_Q$-fixed compatible boundary tuple. Then $(Q-1)r_n=0$ for every $n$. Write the positive integer $Q-1=\ell^a u$ with $a\geq0$ and $u$ prime to $\ell$; this is possible since $Q=q^m>1$. Fix $n\geq1$ and a coordinate $x\in I$. In the compatible bases of step 7, write $r_{n+a,x}=c e_{n+a}$ for $c\in\mathbf Z/\ell^{n+a}$. The equation $\ell^a u c=0$ says that an integer lift of $c$ is divisible by $\ell^n$, because $u$ is prime to $\ell$. Its reduction to $A_n$ is zero. Compatibility therefore gives $r_{n,x}=0$. This holds for every $x$ and $n$, so $r=0$. For empty $I$ the same conclusion holds for the unique empty tuple. This proves the no-nonzero-fixed-element assertion, including the case $\ell\mid Q-1$ where the individual finite levels can have nonzero fixed elements.

source.place: Second paragraph, last sentence: the inverse-limit fixed element is zero
